children.scenario_description: An application submits events that require the framework's event-processing services during normal operation, and the framework processes them completely and exactly as required; response measure unspecified.
children.stimulus: An application submits events that require the framework's event-processing services.
children.response: The framework processes the events completely and exactly as required.

children.scenario_description: Several events arrive one after another while the system is running with its single Event Queue and Event Manager, and the Event Manager dispatches them to their handlers in First-Come-First-Served order; response measure unspecified.
children.stimulus: Several events arrive one after another.
children.environment: Normal operation with a single Event Queue and a single Event Manager.
children.response: The Event Manager dispatches the events to their handlers in First-Come-First-Served order.

children.scenario_description: No input has been received after the system has started, and the system remains in an idle wait state and resumes event processing when input arrives; response measure unspecified.
children.environment: The system has started and is awaiting input via the CLI.
children.response: The system remains in an idle wait state and resumes event processing when input arrives.

children.scenario_description: A request to terminate the system is received during normal operation, and the STOP handler handles it and terminates the system; response measure unspecified.
children.stimulus: A request to terminate the system is received.
children.response: The STOP handler handles the request and terminates the system.

children.scenario_description: A failure occurs in a framework component during event processing in normal operation, and the system recovers and resumes event processing immediately; response measure unspecified ('immediate' is not quantified).
children.stimulus: A failure occurs in a framework component during event processing.
children.environment: Normal operation on a single processor with one Event Manager and one Event Queue.
children.response: The system recovers and resumes event processing immediately.

children.refinement: Handling of user errors and invalid input
children.scenario_description: A user enters erroneous or invalid input through the CLI during normal operation, and the system detects and handles the error and continues to accept input; response measure unspecified.
children.stimulus: A user enters erroneous or invalid input through the CLI.
children.environment: Normal operation, with the system waiting for input.
children.response: The system detects and handles the error and continues to accept input.

children.scenario_description: An event is processed that involves the Main module, Event Queue, Event Manager and handlers during normal operation, and the components interact in a coordinated manner according to their defined interactions; response measure unspecified.
children.stimulus: An event is processed that involves the Main module, Event Queue, Event Manager and handlers.
children.response: The components interact in a coordinated manner according to their defined interactions.

children.scenario_description: Events of the same kind are submitted at different times during normal operation, and the architecture handles them with consistent behavior; response measure unspecified.
children.stimulus: Events of the same kind are submitted at different times.
children.environment: Normal operation with sequential event processing.
children.response: The architecture handles the events with consistent behavior.

children.scenario_description: A new demand on system functionality arises during development or maintenance, and the new application-specific functionality is added to the architecture; response measure unspecified.
children.stimulus: A new demand on system functionality arises.
children.response: The new application-specific functionality is added to the architecture.

children.scenario_description: A developer is asked to modify the framework during maintenance, and the modification is made quickly and cost-effectively; response measure unspecified (no time or cost target is given).
children.stimulus: A developer is asked to modify the framework.
children.response: The modification is made quickly and cost-effectively.

children.scenario_description: A request is made to change the user interface from command-driven (CLI) to window-based during development, and the interface is changed; response measure unspecified.
children.stimulus: A request is made to change the user interface from command-driven to window-based.
children.response: The user interface is changed to a window-based interface.

children.scenario_description: Architects of a future system want to reuse major parts of the framework when developing that architecture, and those parts are reused in the new architecture; response measure unspecified.
children.stimulus: Architects of a future system want to reuse major parts of the framework.
children.response: The major framework parts are reused in the new architecture.

children.scenario_description: A request is made to expand the framework with new components or more sophisticated options during development, and the framework is extended to accommodate them; response measure unspecified.
children.stimulus: A request is made to expand the framework with new components or more sophisticated options.
children.response: The framework is extended to accommodate the new components or options.

children.refinement: Multiple applications at the same time
children.scenario_description: Several applications are hooked up to the framework at the same time, and the framework serves all of them; response measure unspecified.
children.stimulus: Several applications are hooked up to the framework at the same time.
children.environment: Runtime, on a single processor with one Event Manager and one Event Queue.
children.response: The framework serves all connected applications.

children.scenario_description: A user submits input that generates an event during normal operation with sequential processing on a single processor, and the system processes the operation at the fastest possible speed; response measure unspecified ('fastest possible speed' is not quantified).
children.stimulus: A user submits input that generates an event.
children.environment: Normal operation with sequential event processing on a single processor.
children.response: The system processes the operation at the fastest possible speed.

children.scenario_description: An unauthorized party attempts to access the system through its CLI input during normal operation, and the system prevents the access; response measure unspecified.
children.stimulus: An unauthorized party attempts to access the system.
children.environment: Normal operation, with input accepted through the CLI.
children.response: The system prevents the unauthorized access.

children.scenario_description: Data held in framework data structures is accessed from outside its owning component during normal operation, and the data remains properly encapsulated and confidential; response measure unspecified.
children.stimulus: Data held in framework data structures is accessed from outside its owning component.
children.response: The data remains properly encapsulated and confidential.

children.scenario_description: The implementation is moved to a different execution environment, and it executes there; response measure unspecified.
children.stimulus: The implementation is moved to a different execution environment.
children.response: The implementation executes in the new environment.

children.scenario_description: A decision is made to implement the framework in another programming language during development, and the architecture supports that implementation flexibly; response measure unspecified.
children.stimulus: A decision is made to implement the framework in another programming language.
children.response: The architecture supports implementation in the other language.

gaps.description: No response measure is stated in the inputs for any utility-tree scenario: FUN-1, FUN-2, FUN-3, FUN-4, REL-1, REL-2, CI-1, CI-2, MOD-1, MOD-2, MOD-3, VAR-1, VAR-2, VAR-3, PERF-1, SEC-1, SEC-2, PORT-1, PORT-2. All response measures are therefore left unspecified.
gaps.missing_evidence: A stakeholder-stated, measurable response measure (for example a time, count, effort or pass/fail criterion) for each scenario.
gaps.resolution_question: What measurable response would show that each scenario is satisfied?

gaps.description: Scenario PERF-1 (from RS-2) asks for the 'fastest possible speed', which is not a measurable target; the inputs give only a qualitative 'slow' characterization and a component-count proxy, so no latency or throughput threshold exists for PERF-1.
gaps.missing_evidence: A numeric latency or throughput target and a workload description for event processing.
gaps.resolution_question: What response time or throughput, under what event workload, is acceptable for PERF-1?

gaps.description: Scenario REL-1 (from RS-3) requires 'immediate recovery' after any failure, but neither the recovery time nor the kinds of failure in scope are quantified for REL-1.
gaps.missing_evidence: A recovery-time target and a list of failure types (handler, Event Manager, Event Queue, process) in scope.
gaps.resolution_question: Which failures must REL-1 cover, and within what time must the system recover?

gaps.description: Scenario MOD-2 (from RS-7) requires modification to be 'cost-effective, fast and in minimal time', and MOD-1, MOD-3, VAR-1, VAR-2 describe changes without any effort, time or cost bound; no kind of change or effort budget is stated for MOD-2.
gaps.missing_evidence: Representative change requests with an effort, time or cost bound, and the set of components a change may touch.
gaps.resolution_question: Which concrete changes are expected, and what effort or elapsed time is acceptable for each?

gaps.description: No importance or difficulty rating is supplied for any scenario (FUN-1, FUN-2, FUN-3, FUN-4, REL-1, REL-2, CI-1, CI-2, MOD-1, MOD-2, MOD-3, VAR-1, VAR-2, VAR-3, PERF-1, SEC-1, SEC-2, PORT-1, PORT-2), so every priority tuple is null and the scenarios are not ranked.
gaps.missing_evidence: Stakeholder-assigned importance (High/Medium/Low) and architect-assigned difficulty (High/Medium/Low) per scenario.
gaps.resolution_question: Which scenarios do stakeholders rate as most important, and which does the architect rate as most difficult to achieve?

gaps.description: The Performance (PERF-1), Security (SEC-1, SEC-2) and Portability (PORT-1, PORT-2) nodes come only from raw candidate scenarios and style probes; none of these attributes is among the named architectural drivers (Variability, Reliability, Conceptual Integrity, Functionality, Modifiability), so whether they are in scope for the evaluation is unclear.
gaps.missing_evidence: Confirmation from stakeholders that performance, security and portability are quality attributes of concern for this system.
gaps.resolution_question: Should performance, security and portability be treated as drivers for this evaluation, or are those candidate scenarios out of scope?

gaps.description: Scenarios FUN-2, FUN-3 and FUN-4 were derived by the evaluator from runtime and technical constraints (FIFO dispatch, idle wait, STOP handler termination) rather than supplied as candidate scenarios; their wording and relevance have not been confirmed by stakeholders.
gaps.missing_evidence: Stakeholder confirmation that the derived scenarios FUN-2, FUN-3 and FUN-4 reflect intended behavior.
gaps.resolution_question: Do the derived scenarios for FIFO dispatch, idle wait and STOP-handler termination reflect the behavior stakeholders require?
